Hi @nyck33, can you please include an example of the errors you're facing? I'm going to do my best to guess what might be going wrong. Another user recently reported this error:

```
ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

RAPIDS is currently built on CUDA 11, so you need to install a CUDA Toolkit with that major version. Note that it's fine to use a newer _driver_ but the system must have a CUDA 11 _toolkit_.

If this is the error you see, I think there is room for improvement in the docs. Both WSL2 support and pip support are fairly new, so we appreciate your help in reporting this. I'll file a PR to clarify this requirement in the docs here: https://docs.rapids.ai/install#pip-install

In the meantime, I think you have a couple options:

- Install a `cuda-toolkit` package inside WSL that is major version 11 (I recommend 11.8, the most recent minor version of CUDA 11). You can get that from this link: https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-11-8-0-download-archive?target_os=Linux&target_arch=x86_64&Distribution=WSL-Ubuntu&target_version=2.0&target_type=deb_network
  - Note that you want to install `cuda-toolkit` and _not_ `cuda`, because `cuda` will include a driver as well as the toolkit. WSL can have problems if you install a driver package in WSL, because that driver should come from the host Windows machine. This is discussed further here: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/wsl-user-guide/index.html#cuda-support-for-wsl-2

- Install via conda. Installations with conda will come with `cudatoolkit` from `conda-forge`, and that means you don't have to install the CUDA Toolkit into your WSL system.
@bdice that is exactly the problem I was facing but I went ahead and tried to fix it and that error disappeared but I'll try as you say.  Thanks!
